title: Shared Contracts Handbook for Runtime Extensions and Safe Shims
creator: Ava Chen
description: Create an engineering handbook that prescribes how runtime-level contracts evolve across versions and LTS channels, how to qualify and ship safe shims for consumer compatibility, and what automation and telemetry must be in place to gate rollouts. This ticket centralizes decision patterns for breaking vs non-breaking changes, deprecation signaling, and the tooling required to assist downstream migration.
background: As the serving runtime adds new optimizations and kernel changes, consumers (hosted API, Dedicated pools, Private deployments) must be protected from silent regressions. Existing artifacts cover semver and staged rollouts, but we lack a single operational handbook for building 'backwards-friendly' extensions and an automated shim generation + validation flow. This causes ad-hoc migrations, customer surprises, and rollback churn.
goals: (1) Define a deterministic classification of change types (safe, additive, opt-in, breaking) and mapping to version stamp and LTS policies. (2) Produce reviewer checklists and CI hooks that enforce contract tests. (3) Specify runtime shim compatibility patterns and provide a reference shim generator and validation harness. (4) Declare the rollout gates, telemetry signals, and automatic rollback thresholds for canary and gradual rollouts.
non_goals: Not implementing the full shim-generator in this ticket; not replacing product-level API docs. This is a handbook + CI/automation spec with a reference prototype.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Handbook doc reviewed and approved by Release Engineering, Runtime, and Developer Experience. 2) CI checks for contract tests merged into runtime repo (prototype). 3) Reference shim generator repo with example adapter for one kernel change and a walkthrough published. 4) Canary gating rules encoded in deploy pipeline and smoke dashboards added to Console.
decisions: 1) Use three compatibility tiers: Stable (no consumer-facing changes allowed), Extension (additive opt-in features only), and Breaking (requires major bump and migration path). 2) All ABI-affecting or KV-cache-layout changes are Breaking unless accompanied by an auto-translation shim. 3) Deprecations must emit both SDK and HTTP headers for at least two release cycles and be announced in console release notes. 4) LTS channels: stable-lts (18 months support, security/bug fixes only), active-lts (regular backports), and cutting (active feature line).
compatibility_matrix:
- Stable: patch releases only; emergency fixes only.
- Extension: minor releases permitted; behavior gated behind feature flags and opt-in defaults.
- Breaking: major releases; require migration assistant and deprecation timeline.
Mapping examples: configuration field addition -> Extension; field removal or semantics change -> Breaking; kernel reorder optimizing token layout -> Breaking unless shim available.
deprecation_policy: Deprecation flow: announce (release notes + console banner) -> header flag (Deprecated: true, Removal-ETA: YYYY-MM-DD) -> soft-fail telemetry collection (default) -> two minor releases later, hard removal with documentation + migration guide. Minimum notice: 90 days for non-critical, 30 days for critical security removals.
shim_strategy:
- Pattern: implement translation layers at three levels: request (API), transport (HTTP headers/compat flags), and runtime (adapter hooks for kernel differences).
- Reference shim: runtime-shim-refactor prototype transforms old KV key layout to new layout at load time.
- Distribution: shims shipped as compatible runtime modules and as standalone sidecar adapters for Private deployments.
rollout_gates:
1) Unit and contract tests pass.
2) Canary: 1% traffic for 4 hours with golden signal checks.
3) Gradual ramp to 10% for 24 hours, 50% for 48 hours, then 100% if stable.
Automatic rollback if any of the following: error-rate increase > 2x baseline and > 0.5% absolute, p95 latency increase > 30% sustained for 10 minutes, regression in key contract test coverage failures, or customer-impacting errors flagged via support integrations.
telemetry_signals:
- Golden signals: latency p50/p95/p99, error rate, queue depth, saturation (GPU utilization), and tails of batch size distribution.
- Contract telemetry: percentage of requests hitting compatibility shims, shim latency, deserialization errors, and schema mismatch rates.
- Behavioral guards: drift in tokenization metrics or KV cache hit-rate degradation.
upgrade_tooling:
1) migration-assistant CLI (spec) that scans client usage (API fields, flags) and produces a per-consumer migration plan.
2) shim-generator: template-based codegen that produces adapter code for common patterns (field rename, enum expansion, minor shaping).
3) contract-test-harness: lightweight dockerized harness that lets downstream services run runtime contract suites against their integration.
4) release-guard pipeline tasks to run compatibility suite and block merges if critical regressions detected.
migration_examples:
Example A (safe path): Adding optional response metadata -> Extension: no shim required; opt-in flag enabled by consumers.
Example B (breaking): Kernel changes that change KV cache serialization -> generate shim using shim-generator; validate shim with contract-test-harness; ship shim alongside minor runtime then deprecate old layout.
Example C (config rename): provide HTTP header translator in sidecar; log deprecated header and emit migration-assistant report.
reviewer_checklist: - Does the PR include a compatibility classification? - Are contract tests added/updated? - Is a shim prototype or migration plan provided for Breaking changes? - Are telemetry metrics and dashboards appended? - Has release notes and deprecation header been drafted? - Is security review required? If yes, add SR ticket.
runbook_and_rollback: Ship runbook with each rollout: checklist for abort criteria, escalation path (on-call -> Release Eng -> Product), automated rollback commands, and support postmortem template. Rollback must preserve request continuity; for stateful cache layout rollbacks, include data-backfill/compatibility steps.
